question: Does a 20,010-byte synthetic Cirrove DesktopVault value become empty after the same delay that emptied an iCloud session value?
arms: save and immediately read in a new process
read the same item from a new process at least 17 minutes later
remove only the unique synthetic item
endpoint: Record exact value equality without printing the value; distinguish an absent item from a present item with zero bytes using libsecret metadata. A failure in one run is not a failure rate.
prediction: If the desktop Secret Service loses large Cirrove values independent of iCloud, the delayed read will fail; if it survives, iCloud-specific updates or session serialization need investigation. Neither outcome alone proves the cause.

environment.cleanup: Always run the clear phase for this exact synthetic key after the delayed check; leave real Cirrove credentials untouched.

interpretation: This one 20,010-byte DesktopVault value survived independent process reads beyond the 15.2-minute point when a real iCloud session item became empty. It rules out neither intermittent desktop keyring failure nor a difference in iCloud session writes or content. No real credential was used or removed.
